hens_rule_text: Up to 4 chickens allowed with a coop set back at least 50 ft; 5 or more chickens require a 100 ft coop setback. Five is stated elsewhere as a general per-residence cap.
permit_notes: No dedicated backyard-chicken permit was found; keeping is governed by Chapter 6 (Animals and Fowl) setback and corral rules rather than a separate license, but this was not fully confirmed.
setback_notes: Coop or corral must be set back at least 50 ft to keep up to 4 chickens, or 100 ft to keep 5 or more; unclear from search extracts whether this is measured from neighboring homes or from property lines.
coop_rules: Chickens must be kept in a corral, kept sanitary, with feed in rat-proof containers.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
code_section: Code of Ordinances, Chapter 6, Article III (Sec. 6-42, Sec. 6-66 area), amended by Ordinance No. 2017-0-072

research_notes: Municode's Laredo pages are region-blocked from this machine and could not be opened; the 50/100 ft setback tiers and 4-vs-5 chicken split come from a local TV news segment (secondary), and the overall 5-chicken cap and rooster ban come from the same secondary source repeated across chicken-law aggregator sites. The exact code text was not read, so the max_hens figure and setback basis (property line vs. neighboring home) are uncertain.
